notes:
Reached via plain HTTPS fetch, no WAF; robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow. Discovery via homepage mega-menu JSON (editorialContent.content.nav) plus category-sitemap.xml grep for clearance/outlet/last-chance/sale/deal terms. The mega-menu's 'Offers' department tab (categoryId key1) nests four sibling nodes: Shop All Offers (key1-0, umbrella roll-up, excluded), Special Buys (key1-1, excluded, see below), Returns Outlet (key1-2, kept), and Clearance (key1-3, kept, with 4 genuine nested subSubCategories key1-3-0..3: Furniture/Bedding/Sofas & Armchairs/Home Decor Clearance). Verified the department-filtered Clearance children are NOT the same listing recut by name only - fetched each and confirmed materially different product sets (e.g. Furniture Clearance page-1 = dining tables/chests/sideboards; Home Decor Clearance page-1 = artificial florals/diffusers; Bedding Clearance page-1 = duvet/sheet sets) despite two of them coincidentally sharing similar counts with unrelated facets, so kept as separate rows per the no-dedup-by-count-alone rule. 'Last Chance to Buy' (/category/last-chance-to-buy) is a genuine standalone facet-enabled PLP (target term 'Last Chance') found via sitemap; it is NOT present in the mega-menu nav tree, so it is recorded as a standalone row, not nested under Clearance. 'Returns Outlet' (target term 'Outlet') is likewise a standalone sibling of Clearance in the nav, not a child of it, so also recorded standalone. CLEARANCE VS SALE test applied: 'Special Buys' (/category/special-buys, 843 products) meta description 'exceptional products at outstanding prices' - generic promotional bargain wording, no outlet/clearance/end-of-line/permanence signal anywhere on the page -> EXCLUDED. 'Shop All Offers' (/category/offers/all-offers) meta description 'Grab yourself a bargain... shop Dunelm's latest offers... Save up to 50%' -> a temporary/rolling discounts umbrella (title 'Discounted Items - Up To 50% Off'), no clearance-taxonomy language -> EXCLUDED. 'Best Value Deals' (/category/best-value-deals, 728 products) is genuinely ambiguous - it sits as its own department-level nav node (not obviously a Black Friday/seasonal campaign, and 728 products is too large/evergreen-looking to be a flash promo) but the page carries no outlet/clearance/permanent-markdown wording either, only generic templated copy -> recorded per brief instruction with a MANUAL REVIEW flag rather than silently guessing. All qty values are the shell-ssr-data 'totalProducts' JSON figure cross-checked against the matching on-page rendered '<N> results' text (both templates the site A/B-serves were seen and both agreed in every case here).
